# SkillWatch

> SkillWatch is a free, open-source Python CLI that monitors the external web pages AI agent skills and MCP tools point to, and alerts you when the content changes. It exists because those pages can be swapped to contain malicious instructions after a tool has already passed a security scan (a "bait-and-switch" attack). It runs 13 pattern checks on the changed content and complements static scanners; it does not replace them. It runs entirely on your machine, sends nothing to anyone, is open source (Apache 2.0) with no paid tier or telemetry, and is candid about exactly what it catches and misses.

## What it does

- Extracts URLs from SKILL.md files, MCP configs (JSON/YAML), or plain URL lists.
- Fetches each page (with SSRF protection and DNS pinning) and fingerprints the extracted text with SHA-256.
- On the next scan, compares fingerprints. If the content changed, it runs 13 pattern checks and creates an alert.
- Decodes common obfuscation (ROT13, reversed text, hidden HTML comments) before checking.
- Stores everything locally in SQLite. No cloud, no accounts, no cost. Runs periodically via cron or CI.
- Also detects when a tracked skill/config file itself is edited or gains new URL references (`skillwatch sources`, a local rug-pull check), and can emit SARIF for GitHub Code Scanning (`scan --output sarif`).
- Keeps an append-only, hash-chained ledger of what every URL served and when. `skillwatch verify` recomputes the chain, reports any edited, reordered, or deleted entry, and prints the chain head; `skillwatch ledger --export` writes a portable record anyone can independently re-verify. Publish the head externally and re-check with `skillwatch verify --against <head>` to make history up to it tamper-proof (offline; only a hash leaves the machine).

## Honest limits

- Detection is pattern-based and can be evaded. Measured on a synthetic corpus: 21/35 recall overall (60.0%), 11/25 against attacks designed to avoid detection (44.0%), 21/25 precision (84.0%). Against an adversary who is trying to evade it the triage should be treated as decorative; the value is the change alert and the tamper-evident ledger. Attacks phrased as polite requests, stories, or academic language are not caught, because they look like normal text.
- It is a command-line tool for developers and security engineers. It is not yet usable by a non-technical person.
- It runs periodically (cron/CI), not in real time, and does not replace human review of alerts.
- The content ledger is tamper-evident (a naive edit or deletion is caught by `verify`) and independently re-verifiable. A purely local chain alone can be recomputed by an attacker with database write access; anchoring the head externally closes that gap. Anchor either by hand (publish the head, re-check with `verify --against <head>`) or automatically with `skillwatch anchor`, which gets a signed RFC 3161 timestamp under the optional `[anchor]` extra; `verify` then auto-checks every recorded anchor, catching a full-chain rewrite. Only a hash leaves the machine; the core stays offline.

## How it compares

- Snyk Agent Scan, Cisco skill-scanner, and MCP-Scan check the code and descriptions inside AI tools at install time. SkillWatch checks the external URLs those tools point to, over time. Different layers; use them together.

## Install

    pip install skillwatch
